text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

Before I draft, a few questions. The first one matters most.

1. **Can the email say "your own regular cleaner, plus a named backup you'll know ahead of time" instead of "the same cleaner every single time"?** Your new system has a backup, so sometimes someone else will come. Seven of 18 cleaners left last year, so people will also leave again. If the email promises "every single time," the first sick day or resignation breaks that promise. And these customers already left over this exact problem. The regular-plus-backup version is true. It also answers their complaint directly: no more strangers at the door.
2. **How do customers claim the $99 first cleaning?** For example: reply to the email, call a number, or book through a link. Does the offer have a deadline?
3. **After the $99 visit, does the price go back to $165?** I'd rather say so plainly than let it come as a surprise. Saying it up front also lets the email explain the $25 gap compared with the apps (employees, $21/hour, insured every visit).
4. **Who signs it, and what's the company name?** An email from you as the owner usually works better for win-backs than one from "The Team."
5. **Can the email mention the cleaner's name or the customer's old cleaner?** If your system can insert something like "Maria is still with us," that's the strongest line you could have. If not, I'll write it without one.

1. Yes, I can't promise the same cleaner every single time because of sick days and holidays. But make it as strong as you can without saying anything false. I can commit to a regular cleaner plus a named backup for every customer. Also, since we started this in July, only 1 of our 18 cleaners has left.
2. They can reply to the email or call 555-0164. The offer ends December 31.
3. I don't know, I haven't decided that.
4. Me, Lisa Grant, owner of Brightway Home Cleaning.
5. I don't know if our system can do that.

Here's the draft. It's about 150 words, and every claim in it comes from what you told me.

<final_document>
Subject: Your own regular cleaner, and $99 to come back

Hi [First name],

Last year, one of the complaints we heard most was about a different cleaner showing up each time. That was a fair complaint, and we've fixed it.

Since July, every Brightway customer has their own regular cleaner who gets to know their home. You'll also have a named backup, someone you know ahead of time, for sick days and holidays. Nobody you haven't met will turn up at your door.

It's working. Since July, only 1 of our 18 cleaners has left.

We know we cost more than the app services, and here's why. Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay them $21 an hour, and every visit is insured.

To make it easy to give us another try, your first cleaning back is $99. Just reply to this email or call 555-0164 before December 31.

Warmly,
Lisa Grant
Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning
</final_document>

A few notes:

- **What I left out:** The email doesn't say what customers will pay after the $99 visit, because you haven't decided yet. Once you do, add one line saying what regular visits cost. People who left over price will want to know before they book, and they'll trust you more if you tell them up front.
- **"Nobody you haven't met":** This line only holds if the backup is actually introduced to the customer. If you just give them a name, change it to "Nobody you weren't told about will turn up at your door."
- **The old cleaner's name:** If your system can tell you who each customer's old cleaner was, and that person still works for you, add a line like "Maria is still with us and would love to come back." That would be the strongest line in the email.
- **[First name]:** This needs a mail merge. If you can't do one, use "Hi there."
